inclusion_evidence.commit_subject: fix(scorer): map Value to float in mean() like other metrics (#4286) (#4288)
inclusion_evidence.commit_body_excerpt: mean() was the only built-in metric using Score.as_float() instead of value_to_float(). as_float() does float(self.value), so float("C") raises ValueError on the framework's own CORRECT/INCORRECT/PARTIAL/NOANSWER label constants -- even though accuracy(), std(), var(), and stderr() all map those labels via value_to_float(). A scorer that emits a label value with both accuracy() and mean() attached therefore crashed at metric time, losing the whole run's scores. Make mean() consistent with the other metrics: accept a to_float argument (default value_to_float()) and map each score value through it. Behavior for numeric scores is unchanged (value_to_float casts numbers directly); label values now resolve identically to accuracy() instead of raising. Addresses item 4 of #4286 as a standalone fix, independent of the inconclusive-sample design discussion in that issue. Co-authored-by: Charles
